Typical OpenSearch queries (pivots)

  • Host: _index:helk-sysmon-* AND host.name:"lab-win01"
  • IOC IP: source.ip:"10.0.0.5" OR destination.ip:"10.0.0.5"

Best practices

  2. Validate all IOC/report exports before external send
  3. Chain Timeline Builder → Timesketch → incident closure

timesketch.title: Timesketch
timesketch.body:
Timesketch is the platform forensic timeline tool: chronological consolidation of ingested events, exports from HELK or Velociraptor, with annotation and sharing for the IR team.

Access

Import flow

  subgraph sources [Data sources]

    HELK[HELK export /api/helk/export-timesketch]

    TB[CERT Timeline Builder]

Formats & parsers

SourceWorker fileFormat
EVTX / logstimesketch_pipeline.pyNormalized events
CSV timelineparsers/timesketch_csv.py9 mandatory columns (datetime, message, timestamp_desc…)
Plasoingest pipelineAutomatic sketch import

Configuration

  • config/timesketch/timesketch.conf — main config
  • config/timesketch/sigma_config.yaml — Sigma rules
  • config/timesketch/playbooks.json — analyst playbooks

Analyst workflow (lab case CASE-001)

  1. Upload EVTX with case_id=CASE-001 → auto import by ingest-worker
  2. Or HELK panel → Export Timesketch timeline
  3. Or VR panel → Create Timesketch timeline
  4. Open /timesketch/ → sketch linked to case
  5. Apply playbooks, annotate suspicious events
  6. Share sketch link; link observables to TheHive case if needed

Portal pivots

Timesketch timeline buttons in HELK and Velociraptor panels open the sketch for the current case. Grafana: provisioned dashboard config/grafana/provisioning/dashboards/timesketch.yml.

Docs: docs/PORTAL/TIMESKETCH.md. Test: npx playwright test ui-timesketch.spec.ts.

intelligence.title: SOC Assistant
intelligence.body:
Integrated SOC Assistant (portal-ai.js + portal-ai-autonomous.js): local heuristic processing (FR/EN) to generate queries, Sigma rules, dashboards and summaries — no external cloud call. Header button SOC Assistant or Assisted investigation / Autonomous SOC analysis tabs.

Assistant drawer modes

ModeExample inputGenerated outputs
Queryauth failures on lab-win01 24hOpenSearch DSL, Timesketch CSV, search terms
Ruleobfuscated PowerShellSigma YAML, OpenSearch Detection rule
Dashboardauth failures dashboardGrafana dashboard JSON (API save)
Assethostname / IPInventory correlation + volume
Eventevent descriptionClassification, suggested pivots
Analyze rulepasted Sigma YAMLStructure analysis, FP risks, improvements
Correlationmulti-source contextCorrelated intakes/rules terms
Investigationfull NL descriptionSummary, pivots, timeline, export

Options & explanations

  • Extended context — enriches with intakes/rules/modules cache
  • Risk details — Why / How / Risks blocks per result
  • Copy JSON result, ECharts graphs on timelines

Autonomous SOC analysis 2.0

flowchart LR
  SCAN[Auto scan 2 min] --> CACHE[Rules/intakes cache]
  CACHE --> ANOM[Anomaly detection]
  ANOM --> REC[Recommendations]
  REC --> UI[soc-autonomous tab]
  UI --> INV[Assisted investigation link]

Features: periodic scan, incident/anomaly scoring, generated rules, localStorage persistence (cc-soc-autonomous-v2), overview/timeline/recommendations views.

Audit center integration

Hook on audit load: summary enrichment, AI-assisted audit JSON export.

⚠️ Analyst usage rules

  1. Always validate queries and rules before production deployment
  2. Prefer OpenSearch DSL output for FP-Master SIEM
  3. Test Sigma rules in staging, measure false positives over 7 days
  4. Do not treat the assistant as source of truth — corroborate with HELK/OSD/CTI
  5. Documentation demo mode: destructive actions blocked

Files: portal-shared/js/portal-ai.js, portal-ai-autonomous.js, portal-ai.css.

tutorials.title: Tutorials
tutorials.body:
Recommended analyst paths for the FP-Master platform. Default lab case: CASE-001, hosts lab-win01 / lab-linux01. Full detail: docs/PORTAL/SCENARIOS.md.

1. Incident 360° (end to end)

flowchart TD
  A[Create incident CASE-001] --> B[Upload EVTX + HELK option]
  B --> C[Sync helk-findings]
  C --> D[VR offline collection]
  D --> E[Timesketch timeline]
  E --> F[Export IOC OpenCTI]
  F --> G[TheHive case + Cortex]
  G --> H[Close + KB article]
  1. Incidents → create CASE-001, High priority
  2. Ingestion → upload logs, check Send to HELK if needed
  3. HELK → Sync findings → OpenSearch
  4. Velociraptor → offline collection windows-triage-full
  5. Timesketch → consolidate timeline
  6. CTI → export IOC, validate OpenCTI/MISP
  7. TheHive → IR case, observables, Cortex

2. Endpoint 360° (lab-win01)

  1. HELK → Host lab-win01 → Open in HELK
  2. Grafana helk-sysmon — Sysmon activity 24h
  3. VR → playbook windows-triage-full, offline collection
  4. OSD: _index:velociraptor-* AND host.name:lab-win01
  5. MITRE/Sigma pivots, vraptor-windows-full dashboard

3. Threat 360° (IOC)

  1. CTI → OpenCTI campaign context
  2. MISP → correlate events
  3. HELK IOC field → Open in HELK
  4. OS: fp-ti-* + helk-detections
  5. Cortex via TheHive → analyze hash/IP

4. HELK hunting · 5. VR DFIR · 6. TS timeline

See dedicated HELK Hunting, Velociraptor DFIR and Timesketch sections in this documentation. Validation: python3 scripts/helk_full_config_verify.py, velociraptor_full_config_verify.py.

Tool matrix by scenario

ScenarioCERTHELKVROSTSCTI
Incident 360°✓✓✓✓✓✓
Endpoint 360°✓✓✓✓——
Threat 360°✓✓—✓—✓
TS timeline✓✓✓—✓—

Interactive guided tutorial

The button below starts a tour of key tabs (Overview → Documentation → HELK → Velociraptor → SOC Assistant). Also enable Guided path at the bottom of the documentation page.

tiles.inventory: FP-Master catalog: paths, playbooks, parsers, workers, CTI, interconnections.
tiles.arch: Full Docker, Nginx, services and data flow diagram.
tiles.sekoia: Sekoia.IO — assets, rules, ingestion and volume.
tiles.psoar: — incident queue, SOAR workspace, NIST playbooks and purge.

workflow.title: Case management (SOAR)
workflow.lead: Status and severity are set by the CERT analyst — every change is logged.
workflow.log_empty: No actions yet — change status or severity above.

psoar.panel_lead: Security orchestration, automation and response hub: real-time incident queue, investigation workspace, NIST playbooks, IOC scan, forensic report and controlled purge.
psoar.playbooks_lead: Ready-to-use incident response playbooks aligned with NIST SP 800-61. Applied from an incident's 'Tasks & Playbook' tab.
psoar.pb_apply_hint: Applied from an incident's 'Tasks & Playbook' tab.

sel.unchanged: {n} object(s) already match: nothing will be written.

v.sat_sub: An enabled rule whose fields no source produces is imaginary protection. The SIEM never makes this connection.
v.spots: Blind spots — what to collect first
v.spots_sub: Fields required by the largest number of enabled rules and never produced by this tenant. Collecting the first one reactivates all its rules at once.
v.none_inert: No rule proven inert on the analysed sample.
v.val_sub: What each ingested source actually returns in detections. A SIEM counts events and alerts, it never connects them.
v.ingest_sub: Volume measured source by source. Granularity {interval}.

al.new_hint: The rule is created enabled, with its type's default parameters. Adjust them afterwards in the table.
al.no_types: Rule-type catalogue unavailable: cannot create without a type.

bt.running: Replay running — a Sekoia search job has been started…
bt.title: Replay on real data
bt.batch_running: Replaying {n} rule(s) — each replay starts a Sekoia search job…
bt.refused: {n} rule(s) cannot be replayed: their pattern does not translate without approximation.

sd.title: Schema drift — silent rule death
sd.sub: A field stops being populated, events keep arriving, no alert fires — and the rules testing it go dark. This is the failure that never warns you.

sg.title: SAGF — backed governance
sg.sub: What Sekoia is not meant to carry: configuration memory, satisfiability, debt, proven coverage. SAGF ingests nothing, runs no detection, and its removal leaves Sekoia intact.
sg.compliance_sub: These four checks run against the real code on every view.
sg.l11: Alignment — every mechanism knows when to retire
sg.limits_sub: They remain even when everything is verified. A screen showing 20/20 without them reads as a promise of perfection.
sg.mechanisms_sub: Each carries its refutation condition. An irrefutable mechanism is a dogma.
sg.name: Name
sg.console_sub: SAGQL runs inside SAGF, never inside Sekoia: no load is added to the SIEM.
sg.cost: Estimated cost: {n} search job(s) · budget remaining {b}
sg.sovereignty_note: The two sets are disjoint, and a test verifies it. SAGF never becomes the authority on a Sekoia domain.
sg.k_refutable_h: an irrefutable mechanism is a dogma
sg.refuse_note: SAGF refuses rather than guesses: a query interpreted “as best it can” would return a plausible, false result.
sg.nl_sub: Pattern matching, not understanding. On ambiguity, SAGF refuses and offers the possible readings.
sg.families_sub: Those that remain partial are named for what they are.
sg.memory_sub: Three distinct time axes. Without this memory: no counterfactual, no genealogy, no regression detection.
sg.debt_idle: Debt has not been computed in this session yet.
sg.journal_sub: Decisions, evidence and disputes attached to objects.
sg.journal_attr: Attribution is mandatory: a decision with no author or reason cannot later be held against whoever disputes it.
sg.author: Author
sg.mirror_head: What the platform does not know.
sg.fb_coverage_sub: {q} alert(s) qualified of {s} seen. Without this figure every rate is misleading: a precision computed on 2 % of alerts describes the sample, not the rule.
sg.fb_submit_sub: The author is mandatory: a verdict with no author cannot be held against anyone. “undetermined” is a legitimate choice — forcing an answer manufactures false data.
sg.cf_idle: Conflict analysis walks tens of thousands of pairs: it stays on demand.
sg.cf_truncated: Truncated analysis — the result is INCOMPLETE
sg.cf_contradiction_h: one excludes what the other detects
sg.cf_both_h: the only ones that actually cost
sg.cf_unreadable_sub: {n} rule(s) whose pattern could not be read. They are set aside with their reason, never matched “as best we can”.
sg.dac_export_sub: Deterministic export: two calls on the same state produce exactly the same bytes. Without this, a diff shows noise on every run and becomes unreadable.
sg.dac_plan_sub: Paste a target export. SAGF computes what would change — and writes nothing. Applying requires attribution and goes through the bulk engine.
sg.dac_unknown_note: Unknown identifiers are reported, never created: the export does not carry the fields required for a complete creation.
sg.eco_idle: Economic analysis crosses volume, alerts and coverage.
sg.eco_arbitrate_sub: Enter a budget: SAGF proposes a selection and shows what would be lost.
sg.eff_idle: Crosses analyst verdicts, volume and satisfiability.
sg.adv_idle: Weights coverage by actually observed adversary activity.
sg.adv_none: No gap — or no activity extracted.
sg.twin_idle: Simulates the loss of a source, cutting nothing.
sg.har_sub: Freezes a reference corpus, then detects a regression BEFORE it kills rules.

an.title: Analyst extension
an.sub: Inventories, monitoring and internal tags — backed by the Sekoia API, never written into the SIEM.
an.idle: This dashboard queries the Sekoia API on demand: it consumes search quota.
an.nothing: Nothing to report for this measurement.
an.no_write: These actions stay inside the extension: none writes to Sekoia.io.
an.inv_sub: Snapshot of a Sekoia state. Between two captures, the SIEM may have changed.
an.tags_sub: These tags live inside the extension. None is written to Sekoia.io.
an.bulk_hint: Simulate before applying: the bulk engine shows the before/after state without writing anything.
an.nothing_to_apply: no change — the object is already in this state.
an.applied: Written to Sekoia.io. This action appears in the change log and can be rolled back.
an.write_note: These actions REALLY write to Sekoia.io, through the audited bulk engine (simulation, log, rollback). Nothing is ever applied without a simulation shown first.
an.alerting_sub: Unified feed: intake silence and drift, missing or declining log.hostname, API keys created or expiring within 7 days. Each row comes from a detector that already measured and recorded it — this feed only assembles them.
an.alerting_none: No active alert for this filter.

swbtx.Connexion au tenant Sekoia et état du st: Connection to the Sekoia tenant and state of encrypted storage. The API key is entered here and never returned to the browser.
swbtx.Inventaire complet avec volumétrie, base: Full inventory with volume, baseline and health grade — none of these values is exposed by the SIEM.
swbtx.Rechercher une règle, un tag, une source: Search a rule, tag or data source…
swbtx.Rechercher une source, une entité, un id: Search a source, entity or identifier…
swbtx.Seuils dynamiques adossés à la baseline: Dynamic thresholds based on baseline and standard deviation. Simultaneous alerts sharing a cause form a single incident.
swbtx.Surveillance du parc de clés : expiratio: Key estate monitoring: upcoming expiry, revoked keys, permission scope.
swbtx.Sélection par filtre plutôt que par list: Selection by filter rather than by list of identifiers. Every operation is simulated before execution, and each batch can be rolled back.
swbtx.Toute écriture relayée vers Sekoia est j: Every write relayed to Sekoia is logged: who, what, when, with what result. Secrets are never recorded.
swbtx.Volume, part du total, tendance et écart: Volume, share of total, trend and deviation from baseline, source by source. The SIEM exposes none of these measures.
